markdown:
### Key takeaways
- Regulators are clearing cardiac AI faster than trials can test it: only 0.8% of ECG-AI papers are RCTs, and just [3 of 1,357](https://journals.plos.org/digitalhealth/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pdig.0001597) FDA AI devices were tested on patient outcomes.
- Since January 2026, AI coronary plaque analysis has a Category I CPT code (75577), paying over $1,000 in offices, [according to a vendor](https://www.caristo.com/medicare-finalizes-reimbursement-for-caristos-cari-plaque-across-hospital-and-office-settings/).
- Funding is moving toward real-world rollout: the EU's €20M CHAIN network and ARPA-H's ADVOCATE program both pay for implementation rather than accuracy studies.

### What's new
- **Aug 19** — A census of 1,357 FDA AI devices found cardiovascular tools make up about 9%; only 34 devices had registered prospective trials [PLOS Digital Health](https://journals.plos.org/digitalhealth/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pdig.0001597)
- **Sep 9** — Queen of Hearts became the first AI-ECG model with FDA De Novo authorization for STEMI detection; its main evidence is a retrospective registry [TCTMD](https://www.tctmd.com/news/fda-clears-first-ai-ecg-model-acute-mi-detection)
- **Sep 9** — ARPA-H awarded Tempus up to $9.5M for an autonomous heart-failure care agent and a planned multicenter prospective study [Business Wire](https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260909819242/en/Tempus-Secures-Up-to-%249.5-Million-in-ARPA-H-ADVOCATE-Funding-to-Deploy-First-Autonomous-AI-in-Cardiology)
- **Sep 28** — FDA cleared Tempus ECG-MR (510(k)), which flags undiagnosed moderate or severe mitral regurgitation in adults 65 and older; it is the company's fourth ECG-AI clearance [Business Wire](https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260928106625/en/Tempus-Receives-FDA-Clearance-for-its-ECG-MR-AI-Product-Designed-to-Identify-Undiagnosed-Mitral-Regurgitation)
- **Oct 7** — The ESC launched CHAIN (€20M from EU4Health), which will test six AI use cases in 13 countries and give tools "AI passports" [ESC](https://www.escardio.org/news/press/press-releases/from-promise-to-patient-impact-new-european-initiative-aims-to-accelerate-ai-in-cardiovascular-care/)

### Novel gaps
1. **Several AI-ECG alerts on one patient.** Evidence: RCTs are 0.8% of ECG-AI papers; one tool alone had [32% PPV](https://www.medrxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.04.24.25326391). Study: stepped-wedge RCT running several cleared tools; endpoint: confirmed disease per echo ordered. Funder: PCORI.
2. **Skin-tone accuracy of smartwatch (PPG) AF alerts.** Evidence: 4.4% fairness share, the map's lowest; melanin [absorbs green light](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12592569/). Study: prospective, measured skin tone, ECG-patch reference; endpoint: sensitivity by skin tone. Funder: NHLBI.
3. **Children's arrhythmia AI, beyond LV dysfunction.** Evidence: 1.6% of AF-detection papers are pediatric; pediatric AI-ECG performance [varied by hospital](https://www.icthealth.org/news/ai-ecg-helps-target-mri-follow-up-in-repaired-tetralogy-of-fallot). Study: multicenter external validation for SVT and WPW; endpoint: sensitivity versus pediatric electrophysiologists. Funder: NICHD.

*Dropped because already covered: AI-ECG for LV dysfunction in low-resource settings ([prospective Kenya study](https://www.utsouthwestern.edu/newsroom/articles/year-2026/may-ai-powered-electrocardiogram.html)) and autonomous heart-failure agents (ARPA-H-funded).*

### Outlook
With reimbursement and EU and US funding now in place, the next proof cardiac AI needs is better patient outcomes, not higher accuracy scores.
